final.reason: All six full-transient evaluations remained failing, each with 4 faults and 0 delivered-on-time reports. The tested directions included retuning the auxiliary beam toward 210 Hz, minimum trigger threshold, maximum storage with a low start gate, and both longer and shorter effective-length hypotheses for the hidden mounting factor. None produced a delivered report, so no tested design is a feasible selection. I do not claim global INFEASIBLE because the hidden stationary length factor is unrevealed and a failed six-point search is not a full-domain proof. The selected evaluation is the best-tested compromise: main beam left at its nominal 30 mm background resonance, auxiliary beam lengthened to 19.1 mm for target selectivity, 200 uF storage at a 2.7 V start gate for adequate above-brownout report energy, and the trigger threshold at its legal minimum to maximize wake sensitivity.
